The system shall keep OBS Roles distinct from RBAC access roles (Section 3.2); holding an OBS Role shall grant no permission by itself.
The system shall version units, roles, role-function links and Role Assignments under Section 3.8, so the OBS as it was on any past date can be shown, and enforce the quotas of FR-DA-TEN-07.

The system shall link every AI Use Case to the tasks or steps it supports, the link naming the input fields it reads and the output fields it proposes, and shall show the use case only on those tasks and steps (FR-DA-AI-12, FR-DA-AI-13).
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall check each link for fit — the use case's expected output matches the output or a field of the step, and its inputs exist at that point of the process — and flag a link that fails the check for review.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall hold, for every AI Use Case, a Prompt Specification made of separate fields: Role (persona); Context (the process, task or step, the standards and clauses applicable, the Organization profile); Task (the instruction); Inputs (named variables bound to record and step data); Knowledge sources (the corpora and references to retrieve from); Constraints (what the answer must and must not do, including the grounding rule of FR-DA-AI-11); Examples (one or more input and output pairs); Output format (structure, fields, length and a schema where the output fills a form); Tone and language; Quality criteria (how a good answer is judged); Human checkpoint (who reviews and what they check); and Model parameters (model, temperature, maximum length).
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall let an authorized user edit each field of a Prompt Specification on its own, and shall version each change under Section 3.8 with its author, date and note.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall let the user see the history of the whole specification and of each field, compare any two versions, and restore any version of one field or of the whole specification as the new Current Version.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall require, before an AI Use Case can be activated, that Role, Context, Task, Constraints, Output format and Human checkpoint are filled, and shall show the completeness of every specification.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall populate every seeded or AI-suggested use case fully for the task or step it is linked to: the Context shall name that task or step, its inputs, outputs and applicable clauses; the Inputs shall bind to its actual fields; the Examples and the Output format shall match its form; every seeded specification shall be complete (100 %), its Examples holding at least one input and output pair built from the form of the linked step.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall assemble the prompt from the fields in a fixed, documented order, resolve every variable, and refuse to run when a required variable has no value, naming it.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall let an authorized user test a Prompt Specification on a chosen record before publishing a new version, without writing the result to the record.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall record in the AI Usage Log (FR-DA-AI-07) the use case, the specification version, the engine and model used, and the outcome of every run.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall let an AI Use Case be suggested for a task or step that has none — by rule or with AI — as a draft with a fully populated Prompt Specification, activated only after a person reviews it.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall show with every AI answer the engine that produced it (Engine Transparency) and, when the Organization's live model was not used, a visible message giving the reason — no model enabled, or the error the model returned — with a link to the model settings for users entitled to change them.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall make the built-in engine produce, when it answers, content of the type the use case expects (for example a draft text built from the records already captured), never an echo of the input.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall send as prompt inputs only the values the user typed or the records named in the specification, never the state of interface controls (for example the choice made in a list of outcomes).
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall insert an accepted or edited suggestion into the output field the use case names (for example the final validated text), never into an input field.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall let an AI suggestion fill several rows of a record table, each row linked to the records it concerns and marked with the Entry Origin AI, for the user to review, edit or delete before completion.
section: 4.40 AI Use Case Mapping & Prompt Specification

text: The system shall require an explicit name for every task and step, beginning with an action verb followed by its object (for example “Identify the interested parties”), unique within its parent, in every supported language.
The system shall check names on save — missing verb, generic wording, abbreviation, duplicate — and show each finding as a warning that the user may accept or correct.

The system shall give every step a brief (one line, shown by default) and a detailed description (purpose, inputs, how to fill each field, expected result), expandable and collapsible, in every supported language.
The system shall show on every step its process, inputs and outputs, the standards and clauses of the record that it covers, and the rules and controls that apply to it.

The system shall give every step a Step Form Kind from a catalog — at least record table, assessment matrix, decision, objectives, plan, communication, training, monitoring, review, assignment, configuration, document and free record — each with its own fields, checks and completion effects.
The system shall capture lists as tables of rows, one row per item, with add, edit and delete, each row carrying its source (a named record, study, interview or date) rather than free text.

The system shall provide a decision or assessment matrix with criteria, weights, scores on a stated scale and the facts justifying each score, computing the weighted score and showing the scale next to it (FR-DA-HLP-04).

The system shall, when a step is completed, create or update the records it implies — rows of a plan become actions, objectives become entries of the objectives register, KPI rows become KPI values with their alerts — and link each created record back to its row.
The system shall let a KPI be chosen from the KPI catalog, or created in place, with the reason it is monitored, and let people and units be chosen from the OBS (FR-DA-OBS-08).
The system shall validate the mandatory fields of a form before completion, naming each missing field, and lock the step once the gate of its phase is passed (FR-DA-AUD-05 governs reopening).

The system shall show, before a macro process starts, an optional Readiness Checklist: required inputs, completed predecessor processes, owner and RACSI assigned, templates available and KPIs defined. Items the system can verify shall be checked automatically; the checklist shall inform and never block.

The system shall choose the Step Form Kind from the meaning of the step, not only from its object: in particular, a step that maps functions to decision levels shall be a Function × Level Matrix — one row per function of the Organization, one tick column per decision level, an action adding every function not yet listed and an AI proposal derived from the OBS — never a generic list of items with a category and a description.

The system shall, when a step is reopened (FR-DA-AUD-05), clear every completion mark of that step — its step record and the step list of its task — so that the step reads as open everywhere, and record the reopening with its justification.

The system shall keep a library of documented-information templates with full Create, Read, Update, Delete and Duplicate, versioned, each with a code, a category, the formats it produces (Word, PDF, Excel), and ordered sections typed as text, table or approval block.

The system shall let each section be bound to a named data source of the application (for example context issues, interested parties, objectives, KPIs, risks, RACSI, audits, nonconformities, actions), with free text that may use variables such as the Organization name.

The system shall list, per standard in scope, the documented information it requires — to maintain (a document) or to retain (a record) — with the template and the document that answer each requirement, and create a missing one in one action.
The system shall generate a document from a template and the current data of a project, as a draft version, and let it be regenerated from newer data or edited section by section.

The system shall manage document versions through Draft, In review and Published, with approval by a person other than the author (two-person rule) and a change note; one version is published at a time and earlier versions stay downloadable.
The system shall download every document version in each of its formats, with a cover page, a table of contents where relevant, headers, footers and page numbers.
The system shall let an Organization set its document layout — logo, colors, fonts, header and footer — applied to every generated document.
The system shall let an Organization copy a library template to adapt it; its copy replaces the library template within the tenant and keeps the version it came from.
The system shall let a document be retired, with a justification, rather than deleted once published; a draft may be deleted.
The system shall link generated documents to the step, process and project they come from, and show them on that step.
The system shall seed the template library and, in the demonstration data (FR-DA-OPS-09), documents generated for every seeded project, ready to download.

The system shall let a document template set its Document Formatting: body and heading fonts and sizes, alignment, page orientation, margins, cover page, table of contents, heading numbering, page numbers, colors, header and footer.

The system shall let a document template choose its logo (the Organization logo, another uploaded logo or none), the position of the logo on the cover page, and whether the logo appears in the page header.

The system shall let each section of a template or draft document carry its Section Formatting: alignment, text size and color, background (callout), bold, italic, page break before and a hidden title.

The system shall support Picture Sections showing an uploaded PNG or JPEG picture or logo with a caption, a width as a percentage of the page and an alignment; the picture shall keep its proportions and never exceed the page.

The system shall apply the Document Formatting, Section Formatting and Picture Sections in every output format (Word, PDF, Excel), using the organization layout (FR-DA-DOC-07) for any value the template leaves empty.
The system shall preview the Document Formatting while it is edited.
The system shall let a draft document edit its own sections, pictures and formatting without changing the template it was generated from.
The system shall let the user add, move, duplicate and delete sections of every kind — text, table, approval block and picture — in a template and in a draft document.

The system shall produce Word, Excel and PowerPoint files that open in their reference applications without a repair prompt: each package shall pass Office Open XML schema validation, every shape and drawing object of a slide shall have a unique identifier, every chart axis referenced by a series shall be declared, and the package shall hold no directory entries; a release shall check every generated file type automatically.

The system shall draw every value of a generated document from the application's records through a Data Source Binding; the same item shall appear with the same identifier, name and values in every screen and every document that shows it.

The system shall trace every data-bound table row and value of a document to its source record (identifier and version), list the data sources used at the end of the document, and show the date and time of the data ("data as of").

The system shall, when the register a section is bound to has no entry yet, use the records typed in the steps that feed it; when no data exists at all, it shall print a visible notice naming the step or register that provides the data, never an empty section or an empty table.

The system shall define a Document Profile per document type, and each generated document shall carry at least: an identification block (reference, title, version, status, owner, approver, dates, classification, distribution), purpose and scope, references and definitions, method and rating scales where scores are used, the data sections of its type, analysis and conclusions, actions with owner and due date, a revision history and an approval block.

The system shall produce data sections at the finest grain of the data: one row per item, each with its own category, description, relevance or score, owner, dates, status and source or evidence, rather than grouped or summarized text.

The system shall, for a procedure or process description, include the process flow as a diagram (BPMN 2.0 with lanes per role, gateways and exception flows), the inputs and outputs of each activity (SIPOC per step), the decision points with their Go / No-Go criteria, evidence and decider, the records produced, the indicators and the risks and controls.

The system shall run Consistency Checks before a document is sent for review and before it is published: referenced items exist and are current; totals, counts and scores agree with their rows; identifiers and names match the records; every mandatory section of the Document Profile is filled; dates are coherent (next review after last review); and the document agrees with the other published documents of the project that show the same items.

The system shall list the findings of the Consistency Checks with their location in the document and a link to the record to correct; findings marked blocking shall prevent publication, the others shall be accepted with a justification (Section 3.7).

The system shall show, for every published document, whether its source data changed since it was generated, list the changed items, and propose a new version; a data change that affects a published document shall raise an alert to its owner (Section 4.9).

The system shall keep the documents of a project mutually consistent: a change of a shared item (for example a party, a risk, an objective, a process owner) shall list every document that shows it and let the owner regenerate them together.

The system shall lay out each format for reading: a cover page and a table of contents where relevant; landscape pages for wide tables; table headers repeated on each page; no heading or table header left alone at the bottom of a page; diagrams rendered as images in Word and PDF; one sheet per table after a cover sheet in Excel; status values shown with the semantic color scale.
The system shall generate a document in any supported language, with the data in that language, and keep the language of each version.

The system shall keep a master list of the project's documented information up to date automatically: reference, title, version, status, owner, approval date, review frequency, next review, retention for records, and the requirement each document answers.

The system shall support Create, Read, Update, Duplicate and Delete on documents: create from a template or blank, read on screen and in every format, update the metadata (title, owner, approver, review frequency, classification, distribution), duplicate to another project, and delete a document never published; a published document shall be retired with a justification, not deleted (FR-DA-DOC-09).
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall support Create, Read, Compare, Restore and Delete on document versions: create a minor or major version by regeneration from newer data or by copy of the current content; read and download any version; compare any two versions section by section and row by row; restore any version as a new draft; delete a draft version only.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall support, on a draft version, Create, Read, Update, Reorder and Delete on sections: add a section (text, data-bound table, diagram, key-value block, approval block), rename it, move it, delete it, edit its text, and change its Data Source Binding, filters and columns.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall let an authorized user edit a row of a data-bound table from the document through Edit-through — add, change or delete the source record under its own rights, checks and audit — and regenerate the section, so the document and the application stay the same.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall let an authorized user set a Section Override for text or a value that belongs to the document only; the override shall be marked, kept when the document is regenerated, listed in the Consistency Checks and removable to return to the source data.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall keep, when a document is regenerated, the manual text and overrides of its sections, and show the user what the regeneration changed before the new version is saved.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall apply the same CRUD to templates (FR-DA-DOC-01): sections, their order, text, data sources and Document Profile; a template change shall apply to documents generated after it and be offered to existing drafts.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall support Create, Read, Update and Delete on the document layout of an Organization (FR-DA-DOC-07) and on its per-type variants, with a preview, versioned under Section 3.8.
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall gate every document, version, section, row and layout action by its own permission, enforce the two-person rule for approval (FR-DA-DOC-05) and write every action to the audit trail (Section 4.11).
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall show where to customize documents from the documents screen and from every document: templates (all documents of a type), layout (all documents of the Organization) and structure (this document only).
section: 4.45 Generated Documents: Full CRUD at Every Level

text: The system shall qualify every field and column title with the object it holds in its context (for example "External issue", "Interested party", "Macro process 1"), never a generic title such as "Item"; a reusable form shall take its titles from the step or record type that uses it.
The system shall present every choice as a Controlled List with a Custom value that opens a free text field, and shall offer again, in the same list, the values already typed in the same table.

The system shall let the user open any row of a record table in a Row Editor — one large field per column, scrolling, previous and next row, and a return to the table — in edit mode and in read-only mode; a new row shall open in the Row Editor.

The system shall let reference items (processes, phases, functions, people, units, records) be chosen from pickers of the current project or Organization, shown as "ID (name)", with a Custom value where an item outside the application is allowed.
The system shall explain every computed or scored field under the field — what it measures, how it is computed and where it is used — and every free-text field that feeds a document.
The system shall keep the user's unsaved input when a dialog or Row Editor is closed with Back, and ask for confirmation only when the input would be lost.

The system shall support Record Links many to many between records (for example a need or expectation and the interested parties it concerns, a risk and the processes it affects), each end chosen from the records already identified in earlier steps or registers, or typed as a Custom value.
section: 4.47 Linked Records, Choice Libraries & Register Propagation

text: The system shall let multi-valued records be entered in three ways — typed (Manual), taken from a Choice Library (Library) or suggested by the AI (AI) — and record the Entry Origin of each.
section: 4.47 Linked Records, Choice Libraries & Register Propagation

text: The system shall build each Choice Library from the values entered before in the Organization, in any project, together with a reference list managed as configuration data; library values are not linked to any record until the user links them.
section: 4.47 Linked Records, Choice Libraries & Register Propagation

text: The system shall apply Register Propagation when a step is completed: each row of an identification step creates or updates the matching register entry, matched by its identifier or its name, and keeps the identifier of that entry; linked records update the entries they concern.
section: 4.47 Linked Records, Choice Libraries & Register Propagation

text: The system shall keep steps, registers, pickers and documents consistent: an item typed in a step is offered in the pickers of later steps, shown in its register, and printed in the documents bound to that register (FR-DA-DGC-03).
section: 4.47 Linked Records, Choice Libraries & Register Propagation

text: The system shall let the frequency of an audit or inspection be chosen from a list (for example monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual, every two years, every three years) or set as Custom with its description, and derive the next planned date from it.

The system shall record, for each planned audit, its objectives, criteria, scope, processes, duration, lead and team with their qualification, and justify its frequency from the risks and the results of earlier audits.

The system shall grade every finding on a configurable scale — at least major nonconformity, minor nonconformity, observation and opportunity for improvement — with the grading rules shown to the user.

The system shall hold a detailed record for each nonconformity: requirement and clause, statement, objective evidence, process and auditee, root cause, correction, corrective action with owner and due date, verification of effectiveness and status, linked to the corrective action process of the application.
The system shall produce the audit report from these records: summary, strengths, findings by grade and by requirement, one detailed sheet per nonconformity, conclusion and follow-up (Section 4.44).

The system shall choose the entry pattern of each record type from its number of fields, and document the choice: an Inline Editable Table for several records of two to eight fields; Master–Detail for several records of more than eight fields; a sectioned form with progressive disclosure for one record of many fields; a simple form for one record of few fields. The Row Editor (FR-DA-DEU-03) shall remain available from every row of an Inline Editable Table.

The system shall lay out an Inline Editable Table with one row per record and one column per field, a sticky header row, a sticky first column (row number or identifier) when the table scrolls horizontally, and an Add row button always visible below the table.

The system shall show the status of each row in its first column: no mark when clean, an Azure dot when changed and not saved, a spinner while saving, a Green check when saved, and an error marker in the Critical status color when a cell is invalid.
The system shall support the keyboard map of Table 4.49-1 in every Inline Editable Table, keep every cell focusable, and keep focus on the active cell across keystrokes (Section 5.14).

The system shall offer, in a column pinned at the end of each row and revealed on hover and on keyboard focus, the Duplicate row, Insert row below and Delete row actions as 24-pixel line icons, with any other action in an overflow menu. A duplicated row shall copy every value and receive focus on its first editable cell; a deleted row shall be restorable for at least 5 seconds — 10 seconds for a deletion of several rows — from an Undo notification and with Ctrl/Cmd + Z. The deletion of several selected rows shall be confirmed in an accessible dialog stating the number of rows and the Undo period, never stating that the deletion cannot be undone.

The system shall reduce repeated typing: a Duplicate previous row action above the table; carry-over of the categorizing value (for example the PESTLE category) from the row above when the user leaves it unset; and a Controlled List with a Custom value (FR-DA-DEU-02), never free text, wherever a known list of values exists.

The system shall accept the paste of several rows of tab-separated content from a spreadsheet, expanding it into the table (tabs as columns, line breaks as rows), keeping every valid cell and flagging only the invalid ones. FR-DA-MRE-19 to 23 extend this requirement to complete records copied from any external file.

The system shall validate a cell when the user leaves it after changing it — a value typed and then cleared counts as a change — never on every keystroke, never when the user only crosses an untouched cell, never on a new empty row or a new row opened in the Row Editor, and never only on submission; re-validate it on change after a first error; show the error under the cell in 12-pixel Open Sans SemiBold with a 1-pixel border in the Critical status color on its start edge; never reset the value typed; and reflect the error in the row status.

The system shall save each row automatically about 500 milliseconds after the user leaves it, never lose a row on navigation, validation failure, panel change, re-render or refresh, warn before the user leaves a page with unsaved rows, and offer a Save all action whenever a row has pending changes.
The system shall confirm a saved row with a 400-millisecond Green tint highlight and a Green check, and show a running count of the records in Muted text in the form "7 external issues identified."

The system shall let the user resize columns from the edge of their header (minimum 80 pixels), reorder them by dragging the header, sort by a header in three steps (none, ascending, descending), choose the visible columns (the pinned first column cannot be hidden) and pin the first column; these choices shall be kept per user and per table. While a sort is applied, rows not yet saved shall stay at the end, in the order they were added, so that a row never moves while it is typed.

The system shall, where the volume of records warrants it, offer row selection by checkbox (Shift-click selecting a range and the header checkbox selecting every filtered row), deletion of the selected rows after confirmation, and setting one field to the same value on every selected row.

The system shall give every record table a toolbar (search, filter chips, density toggle, column chooser, and a bulk-action bar when rows are selected) and a footer (pagination with "Page X of Y", the record count and the page size). A filter shall be added as field, operator and value, removed on its own or with Clear all, and the number of active filters shall be shown on the filter button.

The system shall not use, for multi-record entry, a dialog opened and closed for each row, repeated form cards for tabular data, a wizard for typing rows, or horizontal scrolling without a sticky first column. A file import (FR-DA-MRE-30) is not the typing of rows and may be organized in stages.

The system shall let the user open every Multi-Entry in a Full-Screen Entry Workspace, from an Expand action (a 24-pixel line icon with the accessible name “Open full screen”) always visible in the toolbar of the Multi-Entry and from the keyboard shortcut of Table 4.49-1. The workspace shall fill the whole viewport above the navigation shell and the side panels; keep in a fixed header the title of the Multi-Entry, its context (for example the project and the step), the record count, the save status, the Zoom Controls and the return action; and show the same records, columns, filters, sort and selection as the page.

The system shall offer Zoom Controls in the workspace: zoom with Ctrl/Cmd and the scroll wheel, or with a pinch on a touch screen or trackpad; a zoom slider; Zoom in and Zoom out buttons; a Fit action that scales the table so that all its visible columns fit the width of the workspace; and Reset to 100 %. The zoom shall range from 50 % to 200 % in steps of 10 %, show its current level as a percentage, keep the active cell in view when the level changes, scale the records area only (never the header, the controls or the dialogs), and be kept per user and per Multi-Entry (TableViewPreference). Without Ctrl/Cmd, the scroll wheel shall scroll the table as it does on the page.

The system shall let the user do in the workspace everything the page allows on the Multi-Entry, so that several entries can be typed, saved, changed and deleted without leaving it: add a row; edit any cell in place; open the Row Editor; duplicate and delete rows with Undo; select rows and apply bulk actions; Save and Save all; filter, sort, resize, reorder and choose columns; and use the keyboard map of Table 4.49-1. Row status, validation, autosave, permissions, quotas and the audit trail shall be those of the page (FR-DA-MRE-03 to 13); the workspace edits the same records as the page, never a copy.

The system shall return the user from the workspace to the page with a single action — one return button always visible at the end of the workspace header, named after the place it returns to (for example “Back to <task name>”, its accessible name including “Return to page”), the identifier and status of that place being shown in the header — or with the Escape key. When a cell is being edited, Escape shall first cancel that edit (Table 4.49-1) and a second Escape shall return to the page; when a menu or dialog is open, Escape shall first close it (NFR-DA-FOC-03). On return, the page shall show every change made in the workspace, with pending rows saved or kept with their pending status (FR-DA-MRE-09), the same row scrolled into view, and keyboard focus restored to the active cell or, when none, to the Expand action; no input shall be lost, and a confirmation shall be asked only when a change would otherwise be discarded. The browser Back action shall also return to the page.

The system shall let the user copy one or several complete records from a word-processing document (for example a Word table, or lines of tab-separated values), a spreadsheet (for example Excel), a CSV or text file, a web page or another application, and paste them into any Multi-Entry, on the page or in the workspace, with Ctrl/Cmd + V or a Paste action: each copied row shall become one record and each copied column one field, starting at the active cell, in the order copied. The system shall read the clipboard as an HTML table, as tab-separated text, or as comma- or semicolon-separated text, and shall add rows below the last one when the pasted rows outnumber the rows below the active cell.

The system shall apply a pasted block directly, with an Undo notification, when its columns match the fields from the active cell and it overwrites no value; otherwise — when it holds a header row, more or fewer columns than the target, columns in a different order, or would overwrite existing values — it shall first show a Paste Preview: the mapping of each pasted column to a field, proposed by header name and then by position and changeable by the user; the columns that will be ignored; the rows that will be added and those that will be overwritten; and the invalid cells, marked. The user shall Apply, adjust the mapping or Cancel. A mapping confirmed by the user shall be proposed again for the next paste into the same Multi-Entry.

The system shall convert each pasted value to its field: dates and numbers read in the user's locale (NFR-DA-I18N-05); a value of a Controlled List matched to its label ignoring case and accents, and otherwise kept as a Custom value (FR-DA-DEU-02); a reference given as an identifier or as “ID (name)” resolved to its record (FR-DA-DEU-04); line breaks inside a cell kept and character formatting removed. Each cell shall be validated like a typed cell (FR-DA-MRE-08): valid cells are kept, invalid cells are flagged with their message and the row status, and no row is ever discarded silently. A paste shall be undone in one action, recorded with the Entry Origin Manual, and written to the audit trail as one operation listing the records created and changed.

The system shall accept up to a configurable number of rows per paste (default 1,000) and apply to every pasted row the user's rights, the Solution Pack quotas (NFR-DA-SEC-08) and the state of the Multi-Entry; it shall refuse a paste into a read-only Multi-Entry or a locked step with a message naming the reason, and skip computed columns, which are recomputed. The server shall check every row of a paste or an import with the same rules as a typed row, including the required values of a new row; an overwrite is checked on the cells it changes.

The system shall let the user copy selected cells, or whole rows with their column titles, from any Multi-Entry, as tab-separated text and as an HTML table, so that they paste with their columns into Word, Excel or another application, and back into another Multi-Entry under FR-DA-MRE-19.

The system shall make every error findable: an Issues list in the toolbar giving the number of errors and, for each one, its row, its field and its message, each opening its cell (or the Row Editor for a hidden field); a “Rows with errors” filter; an error marker in the status column of every invalid row, so that an error scrolled out of view stays visible; and a Retry action per failed row and “Retry all failed”.

The system shall show the save state of the Multi-Entry at all times in its footer — “All changes saved”, the number of unsaved rows or the number of rows with errors — offer a Save all action only while changes are pending, and offer Discard, confirmed in an accessible dialog, which returns changed rows to their saved values and removes new unsaved rows; no confirmation or alert of the browser itself (alert, confirm) shall be used.

The system shall keep a Draft Backup of the pending rows of every Multi-Entry in the user’s browser, versioned and timestamped, written on every change and removed once nothing is pending; on return to the Multi-Entry it shall restore the draft with the notice “Draft restored from <date and time>” and a Discard the draft action. Every saved row shall carry its Row Stamp; a save based on an older stamp shall be refused as an Edit Conflict naming the user who changed the row, with the choice to reload the row or overwrite it with the user’s version, and a restored draft row whose record changed or was deleted since shall be listed with, for each one, the choice to keep the user’s version or take the server version.

The system shall queue, not fail, a save that cannot reach the server: the row shall show “Waiting for the connection”, a banner shall state that the changes will be saved when the connection returns, the save shall be retried with exponential backoff (for example 1, 2, 4 seconds up to 30 seconds) and at once when the device reports the connection again; a save refused by the server (validation, rights, lock, conflict) shall not be retried by itself.

The system shall render, in a Multi-Entry of more than a few dozen rows, only the visible rows and a small buffer (virtual rows), inside a scroll area of fixed height, with uniform row heights while long text is not wrapped and a “Wrap long text” choice; continuous scrolling shall be the default for entry, and pages (“Page X of Y”, FR-DA-MRE-13) shall remain available as a view choice for browsing; the ARIA row and column indexes shall stay consistent with the rows rendered.

The system shall run a bulk paste, import, update or delete as a Batch Operation: batches of 200 to 500 rows (configurable), each saved before the next, a failed batch not stopping the others, a progress indicator announced to assistive technologies with a Cancel action between batches, and a Resume action continuing from the first batch not done; a bulk change made on screen (for example a field set on every selected row) shall be sent about two seconds after the last change.

The system shall import rows from a file in an Import Session of five stages shown in a stepper: (1) template — the formats accepted (spreadsheet workbook, delimited text, paste), the limits, and a downloadable template with the column titles, required ones marked, and an example row; (2) upload — drag and drop, file picker or pasted text, with the type, size, row count and text encoding checked and the first ten rows previewed; (3) column mapping — titles recognized, columns matched by position otherwise, every match changeable with sample values shown, and the next stage refused while a required field has no column; (4) error repair — the rows needing attention listed first with their count, each cell corrected in place and checked again at once, duplicates within the file and against the existing rows flagged, guided corrections for the common errors (fill an empty required column, replace a value not in a list, leave the duplicates out) and any row left out on request; (5) summary — the rows ready, with a warning, with errors and left out, the choice to leave rows with errors out or import them as rows to correct, an optional value given to every imported row, the commit as a Batch Operation (FR-DA-MRE-29) and its result with an Undo action for at least 60 seconds. Cancel shall be offered at every stage, confirmed once data was loaded, and moving between stages shall keep everything entered.

The system shall export the current view of a Multi-Entry — its filters, sort and visible columns — or only the selected rows, as delimited text (UTF-8 with byte-order mark) and as a spreadsheet workbook, with the grid’s column titles and display values, the file named after the Multi-Entry’s parent and the date (<parent>-<yyyy-mm-dd>), and spreadsheet formulas neutralized (NFR-DA-SEC-21).

The system shall ask, when the user leaves a page that holds rows not saved — a link, the browser Back action, closing or switching a panel, closing the browser tab — with three choices: Save and leave, Discard and leave, or Stay on the page, stating the number of rows and of rows with errors and keeping the user on the page when rows could not be saved; returning from the Full-Screen Entry Workspace to the page shall never ask, nothing being lost there (FR-DA-MRE-18).

The system shall keep a Multi-Entry readable without horizontal scrolling: when it has more than six columns, optional long-text columns shall be shown in the Row Editor rather than the table until the user shows them (the column chooser stating it); the footer shall show the totals of the number columns, the number of rows shown and selected; the Row Editor shall offer Save and new; and an empty Multi-Entry shall offer Add the first row, Import, Paste and, where an AI Use Case serves it, Propose with AI.

The system shall show, below a phone breakpoint (768 pixels wide by default), no grid but a read-only list of the rows with their status and first fields, an “Edit one by one” action opening the Row Editor with previous, next and Save and new, Add row and Import; errors shall be shown on each listed row.

The system shall undo and redo, with Ctrl/Cmd + Z and Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + Z and with toolbar actions, every change of a Multi-Entry as one step each — a cell edit, an added, inserted or duplicated row, a deletion, a value set on the selected rows, a fill down and a paste or an import — the server following the rows (a row brought back by Undo is restored or created again; a paste or an import is undone as its audited operation).

The system shall let the user resize the navigation panel and the context panel by dragging their edge or with the keyboard (arrow keys by 16 px, Home and End to the limits), within limits (navigation 180–480 px, context 220–560 px, content at least 400 px), and reset a panel by double-clicking its edge; the content panel shall take the remaining width and never have a fixed width.
The system shall apply the default, minimum and maximum widths of Table 4.50-1 and, when the window is resized, clamp the side panels so that the content panel never drops below its minimum width.

The system shall place a drag handle on the inner edge of each side panel, show a resize cursor and a 2-pixel Azure highlight on hover and while dragging, and suspend text selection and pointer interaction in the panels during the drag.

The system shall make each handle keyboard-operable: focusable with a visible focus ring, the left and right arrows changing the width by 16 pixels, Home and End setting the minimum and maximum width; the handle shall expose the separator role, its vertical orientation, its current, minimum and maximum values and a label such as "Resize navigation panel".
The system shall reset a panel to its default width when its handle is double-clicked, and may offer a button that collapses a side panel.

The system shall store the panel widths as a user preference with the other shell preferences (FR-DA-NAV-06), cached in the browser for an immediate layout, and clamp them to their limits when they are applied.
The system shall disable resizing below 768 pixels of viewport width and fall back to a single-pane layout (FR-DA-NAV-08).
The system shall treat the start and end panels as logical sides, so that under a right-to-left language the panels, their handles and the directional icons are mirrored (FR-DA-NAV-07).
The system shall choose the chart type from the purpose of the figure, as in Table 4.51-1, and shall never use a pie chart or a three-dimensional chart.

The system shall draw the primary or current series in solid Azure, a comparison or prior period in dashed Muted, a growth or positive trend in solid Green and an overlay or secondary metric in solid Teal, with gridlines in Line; it shall never use the default palette of a chart library, a rainbow palette, gradients, shadows or 3D effects on data.

The system shall label axes in 12-pixel regular Muted text and values in 12-pixel SemiBold Navy text, place the legend below the chart, horizontally, with dot markers, and give every chart a short italic caption in Muted below it.

The system shall resize charts with their container, with a minimum height of 240 pixels, show a skeleton of the chart's size while loading and an icon with "No data for this period." when there is nothing to show.

The system shall show a single indicator as a KPI Tile: a card with 24-pixel padding, the label in 13-pixel Open Sans SemiBold uppercase Muted, the value in 36-pixel Montserrat Bold Navy, the change in 12 pixels with an arrow icon (Green when favorable, the Critical status color when unfavorable) and an optional 24-pixel trend line.

The system shall draw maturity heatmaps with the five Status Scale colors in their fixed order, label every row and column, never color a cell outside the scale, and show the level as text or a number in each cell so that the meaning does not rest on color alone.

The system shall let the user, within the export rights of the user's role, copy a chart as an image, download it as PNG at twice its resolution or as SVG, download the CSV of its underlying data, and print it in a print-friendly rendering.
The system shall give every chart a text alternative and a data-table view reachable by keyboard, and under a right-to-left language mirror the axis origin without reversing the data.

The system shall show a list of more than 20 records by pages, with a Page Size of 20 (default), 50, 100 or all, the range shown (“1–20 of 345”), previous and next and “Page X of Y”; the chosen Page Size shall be kept for the user.
The system shall scroll a table inside its own frame, horizontally and vertically, with a sticky header row and a sticky first column; the page itself shall never scroll sideways.
The system shall sort a table by a column header in three states — none, ascending, descending — with a visible indicator of the current state.
The system shall let each user choose the Density of tables, comfortable (default) or compact, and keep the choice for that user.
The system shall highlight the row under the pointer, alternate the row backgrounds and draw thin, non-black borders.
The system shall give every table a loading state, an empty state with its create action, a filtered-empty state with Clear filters and an error state with Retry (FR-DA-STA-01, 02).
The system shall let the user resize the columns of an editable table (minimum 80 pixels) and keep the widths for that user.

The system shall show a skeleton of the main content region while a page loads, a spinner inside the button that started an in-page action (the button disabled, the page not blocked), and a progress bar with an estimated time for a long operation.

The system shall show an empty state centered, at most 400 pixels wide, with a 48-pixel Muted icon, a title, one sentence and the primary action, leading with the action rather than an apology (for example "No surveys yet. Create your first assessment."); a filtered list with no result shall offer Clear filters, and a failed load shall offer Retry.

The system shall report an error at the level where it occurred: under the field for invalid input, in a notification for a transient failure (network, saving), on a full page with a headline and a primary action for a missing page or a server error, and in a dialog offering "Sign in again" when the session has expired.
The system shall confirm success with a notification for a background operation, an inline check for a row of a table, and a full-page summary at the end of a multi-step process.

The system shall show notifications at the bottom end of the screen on desktop and at the top center on mobile, with an 8-pixel radius and the card shadow, in four variants (information in Azure tint, success in Green tint, warning in the Developing status color, error in the Critical status color, all with Navy text), for 5 seconds by default and until dismissed for an error, with an optional action such as Undo.

The system shall show a persistent banner while the device is offline ("You're offline. Changes will sync when you're back."), queue the user's changes locally and synchronize them on reconnection, where the screen supports offline work (for example Face-to-Face questionnaire capture, Section 4.36).

The system shall present a capability the user may not use in one of three ways, chosen per capability: hidden; visible but disabled with a tooltip explaining why; or, for a whole screen, the access notice of FR-DA-RBAC-08 with a Request access action.
Dashboard and list views shall render within 2 seconds under nominal per-tenant data volumes.
An AI agent suggestion shall return within 5 seconds under its deterministic path.
A knowledge-base or FAQ retrieval search shall return ranked results within 1 second for a tenant's full corpus.
A single standard-report export (PDF, Excel, or Word) shall complete within 3 seconds for a tenant's current data volume.

With 100 concurrent users on one tenant, the 95th-percentile response time of read endpoints shall stay at or below 1 second, measured by a repeatable load test. A per-user read cache, where used, shall hold an entry for no more than 30 seconds and shall be invalidated by any write in the same Organization.
Activating a vertical, with its processes and configuration, shall complete within 5 minutes (configurable target).
A bulk data import shall load 10,000 records within 30 minutes, and an SME shall be able to complete onboarding within 30 days (configurable targets).

A production deployment offering the Vertical and SME layers shall be sized for configurable targets, by default 1,000 API calls per second sustained and 10,000 concurrent users, with reports generated within 60 seconds.
The global search shall show its first suggestions within 300 milliseconds of typing and full results within 1 second at the 95th percentile, for a tenant's full data volume.
Restoring a version of a process element with up to 1,000 descendants shall complete within 5 seconds; generating a document of up to 50 pages from a template shall complete within 10 seconds.

Generating a document of up to 50 pages with diagrams (for example BPMN flows) shall complete within 15 seconds, and the consistency checks of a project's documents within 30 seconds, at the 95th percentile.

A long list shall render at most the selected Page Size of rows at a time (FR-DA-TBL-01); opening a project template blueprint of up to 1,500 steps shall take less than 1 second on the server and less than 2 seconds to display.

The Full-Screen Entry Workspace shall open within 1 second for a Multi-Entry of up to 1,000 records; a zoom change shall be rendered within 100 milliseconds; the Paste Preview of 1,000 rows shall appear within 2 seconds and applying it shall complete within 5 seconds, at the 95th percentile.

A Multi-Entry of 10,000 rows shall open within 2 seconds and scroll and accept typing without visible delay (a keystroke shown within 50 milliseconds), and an import of 1,000 rows shall be committed within 10 seconds, at the 95th percentile.
All API endpoints except login shall require a valid, signed, time-boxed authentication token.
Passwords shall be stored only as salted cryptographic hashes; plaintext passwords shall never be logged or persisted.
Every authorization decision shall be enforced server-side; client-side permission and Pack-entitlement checks are a UX convenience only, never the security boundary.
No data query shall be constructed by concatenating untrusted input; all data access shall use parameterized statements or an equivalent safe-query mechanism.
Owner/Evaluator segregation of duties, and any equivalent server-enforced business rule, shall be enforced server-side, not merely hidden in the UI.
A one-Accountable-per-RACSI-activity rule, and any equivalent uniqueness rule, shall be enforced by a data-persistence-layer constraint, not merely by disabling an option in the UI.

A Real LLM Provider Connection's API key shall be captured and stored only client-side; the backend shall never persist it to any table, write it to any log line, or return it in any API response, and any server-side proxying of a forwarded key shall use it for exactly one outbound call and never write, log, cache, or hold it beyond that request.

Every quota check (Projects, OBS nodes, AI Use Cases, and any other Pack-bound dimension) shall be enforced at the point of creation/activation on the server, never solely by disabling a client-side control; an over-quota request shall be rejected with HTTP 409, never silently truncated or partially applied.

Solution Pack entitlement shall be treated as an authorization axis independent of, and enforced in addition to, RBAC permissions; a route gated by both shall require both checks to pass, each independently testable and independently capable of producing a 403.

Individually identifiable records requiring restricted visibility (e.g. individual-level readiness or sentiment data) shall be restricted, by RBAC default, to an explicitly named set of roles; other roles shall see only aggregated, de-identified views.
Tenant data isolation shall be verified by an automated cross-tenant access test suite exercised in the build/release pipeline, not solely by code review.

The login endpoint shall be rate-limited per client, and every response shall carry standard security headers (content-type sniffing protection, frame protection, and a restrictive cross-origin resource policy).

Caches, backups, and logs shall never make one tenant's data available to another; backups shall be stored outside every web-served directory and be readable only by the service account and the platform administrator.
The system shall support standard federated authentication (SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect) and multi-factor authentication.
Role-based access control shall support scopes by vertical and by SME track in addition to the tenancy scopes.
Data shall be encrypted at rest (AES-256 or equivalent) and in transit (TLS 1.2 or later), with configurable data residency regions and optional customer-managed keys (bring your own key).

An Organization-level live-model key (FR-DA-AI-16) and any integration secret stored on the server shall be encrypted at rest with authenticated encryption (for example AES-256-GCM) under a key held outside the database; it shall never be returned in full, logged, cached beyond its request, exported or included in a backup restore to another tenant. NFR-DA-SEC-07 continues to govern a personal connection.
A search result, count, suggestion or snippet shall never reveal a record, a title or a value that the user could not open on its own screen.

A generated document shall contain only data the requesting user may read; a document shared or downloaded shall carry its classification and shall not include hidden data (comments, hidden sheets, metadata) beyond what it shows.

Picture uploads (FR-DA-DFP-04) shall accept PNG and JPEG only, up to 5 MB, stored under generated, per-tenant names on validated paths; every formatting value (font, size, color, alignment, position) shall be checked on the server against its list of allowed values.

Pasted content shall be treated as untrusted input: markup, scripts, styles, embedded objects and images on the clipboard shall be discarded, never rendered or stored; a text value beginning with =, +, -, @, a tab or a carriage return shall be stored as text, never evaluated, and neutralized when exported to a spreadsheet or CSV (formula injection); and every pasted row shall pass the same server-side validation, authorization and tenant checks as a typed row.

An imported file shall be treated as untrusted input: its type checked by extension and by content, its size and row count bounded by configurable limits, its text read as UTF-8 or, when it is not valid UTF-8, in a stated fallback encoding that the user can change; a spreadsheet workbook shall be read on the server keeping only cell text (the last value of a formula); the rights, quotas and checks of a paste (FR-DA-MRE-22) shall apply to every imported row.

The system shall degrade gracefully if an AI agent or live-LLM call fails: the underlying CRUD operation shall still succeed, with the AI suggestion simply unavailable or served from its deterministic fallback.
The system shall target 99.9% uptime in a production deployment.
A report-export failure shall return a structured error without corrupting or partially writing the underlying report data view.
The persistence layer shall support scheduled backup with a defined retention policy; a production deployment shall not rely on a single unreplicated data file as its sole durability boundary.
The backup schedule shall bound data loss to at most 24 hours, and restoring a backup shall be tested at least once per release.

A production deployment offering the Vertical and SME layers shall support disaster recovery with an RTO under 4 hours and an RPO under 1 hour, automatic failover and automated backups, tightening NFR-DA-REL-05 for that deployment.
Every version of a versioned entity shall be stored complete and checksummed, so that viewing or restoring it reproduces its exact content; a failed restore shall leave the Current Version unchanged.

Generating a document twice from the same data and template version shall produce the same content; every published document version shall keep the data snapshot it was generated from, so it can be reproduced.
A page shall never stay blank: a failure to load or render shall show the full-page error state with a headline and a primary action (FR-DA-STA-03).

Inline data entry shall never lose a row: every row typed shall be saved, or kept with its pending status, across navigation, validation failure, panel change, re-render, refresh, crash of the browser and loss of connection (FR-DA-MRE-09), by the Draft Backup (FR-DA-MRE-26), the offline queue (FR-DA-MRE-27) and the Leave Guard (FR-DA-MRE-32).
A save shall never overwrite a newer version of a record without the user’s explicit choice: every save of a row shall be checked against its Row Stamp (FR-DA-MRE-26).
The architecture shall support horizontal scaling of the web tier independently of the API tier.
The system shall support at least 100 concurrent users per tenant without functional degradation.
The persistence schema and the retrieval index shall each be swappable for a distributed equivalent (e.g. a managed relational database, a vector database) without changing the API contract.

The system shall scale to configurable limits, by default 1,000 tenants per deployment including 10,000 SME tenants in shared mode, 100 million records, 500 macro processes, 200 E2E processes and 100 checklist items per gate.
Adding a vertical, an SME track, a template, a gate or a checklist shall require no downtime.
The UI, and every generated document, shall follow the common visual identity (Section 5.13) (color palette, typography, iconography) consistently across all modules and output formats.
The UI shall be responsive and usable on desktop, tablet, and mobile viewport widths, with touch-target sizing meeting WCAG 2.1 AA on mobile.
All interactive controls shall be keyboard-navigable and carry accessible labels (WCAG 2.1 AA target).
Status, severity, and classification fields shall use one consistent color/badge vocabulary across every module, so a user who has learned a meaning in one module recognizes it in every other.
Every interactive target shall measure at least 24 × 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8), and at least 44 × 44 CSS pixels on touch screens.

Every release shall pass an automated accessibility scan (e.g. axe-core) of its main screens with no critical or serious violation. Text shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast (4.5:1, or 3:1 for large text); where a brand color falls short, its darker tone shall be used for text, and any remaining brand conflict shall be recorded in Appendix A.

Every confirmation, warning, and error message shown as a transient notification shall be translated (FR-DA-I18N-07), announced to assistive technologies through a polite live region, and remain readable long enough to act on.
Wide matrices and tables shall scroll inside their own container, keeping the first column visible, so the page never scrolls horizontally on a 390-pixel viewport.
SME users shall complete onboarding within 1 day and need less than 4 hours of training, helped by guided workflows (configurable targets).
User satisfaction shall be measured, with a configurable target (default NPS of 30 or more).
Search shall be fully keyboard-operable (shortcut, arrow keys, Enter, Escape), group its results by type, highlight the matched words, and mirror under right-to-left languages.
Every step shall show a one-line brief with an expandable detailed description, and every form field shall show how to fill it, in the user's display language.
Every dialog shall keep its title and actions in view and scroll its content with a visible scroll bar; read-only text shall be shown in full rather than inside a small scrolling box.

Every identifier shown to a user shall be followed by the name of the item it identifies, in the form "ID (name)" — for example a phase, a process, a step, a function or a record — in lists, pickers and headers.
A computed field shall be read-only, show how it is computed and why it exists, and never be typed.
Text fields shall be sized for their content; a field meant for more than one sentence shall offer at least five lines, in the form or in the Row Editor.

Every icon-only button shall carry an accessible name; every form field shall have a label bound to it; errors shall be announced through a polite live region; table headers shall declare their scope; dialogs shall trap focus and return it on closing.
Meaning shall never be carried by color alone: a status shall show its label or level, a comparison series shall be dashed as well as grey, and an error shall show a message as well as a red border.

Brand colors shall be applied with the contrast table of Appendix J: Navy, Ink and Muted for any text; Azure only for large bold text and interface components (3.9 : 1); Teal and Green for fills only (2.9 : 1 and 2.2 : 1).

The Full-Screen Entry Workspace shall be accessible: announced to assistive technologies as a labelled dialog, it shall move focus to the active cell on opening, keep focus within it and return focus on leaving (NFR-DA-UX-17); every Zoom Control shall be a labelled button or slider operable by keyboard, with the zoom level announced; the workspace zoom shall complement, never replace or block, the zoom of the browser (WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.4 and 1.4.10); its opening and closing transitions shall last 200 to 300 milliseconds and be removed when the user prefers reduced motion (NFR-DA-VDS-16); below 768 pixels it shall show the records as the mobile page does, with pinch zoom; and under a right-to-left language the workspace, its controls and its return action shall be mirrored (FR-DA-PNL-08).

Every Multi-Entry shall follow the W3C ARIA grid pattern: grid, row, column header and grid cell roles, row and column indexes kept consistent with virtual rows and pages, the sort state of each column announced, a live region announcing the rows added, deleted, saved and failed, batch progress and a restored draft; errors shown with an icon and text, never by color alone; focus moved to a sensible cell after an addition or a deletion; focus trapped only in dialogs; and animations removed when the user prefers reduced motion.
Every layout — navigation, tables, and charts — shall render correctly mirrored under Arabic RTL, not just with mirrored text direction.
The system shall support configurable languages (default English, French, Arabic, Spanish, German), currencies (default USD, EUR, MAD, ZAR) and regional date, time and number formats.

Labels, buttons and headings shall accommodate text 30 % longer in French and 20 % longer in Arabic than in English without clipping, and headlines shall be kept short so that they survive translation.

Under Arabic the layout shall be mirrored in full: the navigation panel moves to the right, chevrons and arrows and every icon with a direction are reversed, icons without a direction (search, settings) are not, and numbers, code and Latin brand names stay left to right.

Dates, numbers and currencies shall be formatted by the locale of the user (for example fr-FR, ar-MA) through the platform's internationalization services; Eastern Arabic numerals shall be used only where the locale requires them; amounts shall show the currency's ISO code with the symbol of the locale.
No text shall be part of an image; idioms and culture-specific references shall be avoided in interface text.

Files exported or downloaded shall keep non-Latin text intact: delimited text in UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, and a file name with non-Latin characters sent in its encoded form (RFC 6266, filename*=UTF-8''…) with a Latin fallback, so that a download never fails because of the language of its name.

Installation shall succeed on a fresh target machine with only a supported Node.js runtime installed — no native C/C++ build toolchain, no required external database server, and no mandatory external API key.
The same source shall run unmodified across supported operating systems via standard package-manager install/build/start commands.

Every change shall be built by a continuous-integration pipeline on Linux, Windows, and macOS that installs dependencies, seeds the demonstration data, runs the automated tests — including the cross-tenant suite of NFR-DA-SEC-11 — and builds the web client.
Each tier shall install, seed, and start with its package manager's standard commands (install, seed, dev or start), documented in a README at the root of the delivery.

The continuous-integration build shall run automated tests of the multi-record entry logic (validation, undo and redo, batching with failure, cancellation and resumption, draft restore and conflicts, column mapping and error repair, export, retries) and an end-to-end import from file upload to commit and undo; test suites that share one database shall run one after another, so that no test fails for a lock.

Cross-cutting engines — the Action/Task Register, the Alert & Notification Engine, the RBAC layer, the KPI/Reporting engine, and the Audit Trail Service — shall be implemented as composable modules reusable by sibling applications via the same API contract.
AI agent implementations shall be isolated behind a stable internal interface so a rule-based implementation can be replaced by an LLM/vector-DB-backed one without changing calling code.
The Solution Pack feature and quota matrix shall be defined in exactly one place and consumed by every enforcing route, so entitlements can never drift between routes.

The AI Use Case Library's generation service shall be the single designated server-side integration point for a live LLM call and its provider-specific credential/endpoint logic; no other module shall embed its own LLM provider client; and no module shall produce an AI suggestion, even from the built-in engine, outside an AI Use Case (FR-DA-AI-23).
The alert type-to-name and type-to-stage/process mapping shall be defined in exactly one shared module, consumed by both seed data and live computation.

The Installation Guide and User Guide shall be generated from source in Word and PDF, each with an automatic table of contents, and the User Guide's step-by-step walkthroughs shall be replayed automatically against a freshly seeded instance, so the documentation cannot drift from the application.

Every User Guide walkthrough shall start from the tenancy — create or choose the Group (Yes/No), create the Organization, then the principal record(s) — and the guide shall include the decision matrix of FR-DA-HLP-04.

Verticals, SME tracks, complexity criteria, packs, project templates, gates and checklists shall be configuration data loaded without code changes, and the platform shall be modular with zero-downtime upgrades, monitoring, alerting and comprehensive logging.
The process design, functions, OBS roles, Prompt Specifications, step form kinds and documented-information templates shall be configuration data, changed without code changes or downtime.
Controlled Lists, Document Profiles, step-specific field titles and data source bindings shall be configuration data, changed without code changes or downtime.

An upgrade shall migrate the data of an existing installation in place at its first start — changed entity definitions, completed catalogs, new fields with their derived values — each migration idempotent, versioned, recorded with what it changed, and run once; an upgrade shall never require the data to be reseeded, and its release notes shall state that the server is restarted after the files are replaced.
The application shall target evergreen desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers; no legacy-browser support is in scope.

BPMN diagrams shall be stored and exchanged as schema-valid BPMN 2.0 XML, verified by a round-trip import/export, so a diagram authored in one application opens without error in any other BPMN 2.0-compliant tool, and vice versa.

The application's core workflows (record CRUD, approvals, alerts) shall remain fully usable on a mobile viewport without requiring a separate native application; a native or installable Progressive Web App wrapper, where offered, shall consume the same REST API (Section 7.2) with no mobile-specific endpoint variant.
Every AI-generated suggestion shall be logged with a confidence indicator and be attributable to a specific agent/use case and record, or, for the AI Assistant, to the requesting user and question.
The Controls module shall support demonstrating COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework coverage across all five components.
The system shall retain the full version history of every AI Use Case and every template indefinitely (no hard deletion of prior versions on edit or revert).

The system shall never represent, in any UI text, Help content, FAQ answer, or generated document, that activating a Compliance & Security Standard constitutes a certification, an external audit, or a legal attestation of compliance.

The system shall let verticals map to sector standards — for example IATF 16949 (automotive), AS9100 (aerospace), EU MDR and ISO 13485 (medical devices), FDA 21 CFR Part 11 (pharmaceutical), HACCP (food safety) — as scaffolds subject to FR-DA-CFG-09; certification (ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, GDPR) is an attribute of a deployment, not of the software.

Every requirement of an application shall be traceable to its business requirement, user story, test case, release and, where applicable, customer commitment, in line with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148; requirement changes shall be classified Minor, Moderate, Major or Breaking with the matching approval and regression scope.

By default, and whenever no Real LLM Provider Connection is configured, the system shall not transmit tenant data to any third-party service; every AI capability shall run entirely within the deployment's own infrastructure using rule-based/statistical methods and RAG grounding. Only an explicitly user-configured, client-stored Real LLM Provider Connection may cause a single generation request to be sent to that user-selected third-party provider — opt-in per user, never enabled by default, and never applied to a permission-scoped data-query mode.
The system shall support both shared-infrastructure (SaaS) and dedicated/sovereign deployment options per Organization, without changing the tenant-isolation guarantee.
A questionnaire response shall be stored within 2 seconds of submission, at the reference load of Section 5.1.
Questionnaire response data shall be retained according to the tenant’s retention policy, by default 5 years, and then deleted or anonymized.
For a questionnaire marked anonymized, the system shall strip the respondent’s identity before storage, so that no stored response can be linked back to a stakeholder.

Every color, font, type size, spacing, radius, shadow, focus ring, duration, easing, breakpoint, panel width and layer of the user interface shall come from the design tokens of Appendix J, defined once as CSS custom properties prefixed --aiv- and never written as a raw value in a component. An automated check in continuous integration shall reject a raw color value outside the token file.

The interface shall be light: page background in Background (#F5F8FB), surfaces in White, borders and dividers 1 pixel in Line (#E1E8F0), never black and never heavy. Dark mode shall not be the default; a dark background shall appear only as a deliberate section divider. The Azure–Teal–Green gradient shall appear only in the logo swoosh and in at most one hero element per page, never on data, charts or text; purple, pink and rainbow gradients shall not be used.

Body text shall be in Ink (#2C3E50) or Navy (#123A5F), metadata and captions in Muted (#5A6B7B). Azure, Teal and Green shall be used for fills, borders, buttons, badges, icons, charts and large bold text (at least 18.66 pixels bold or 24 pixels) only, never for smaller text on a light surface (Appendix J, color contrast).

Status, health, maturity, audit and severity values shall use the five Status Scale colors in their fixed order, always together with a text label or level number, and no other color; this applies NFR-DA-UX-04 across every module.

Headings and KPI values shall be set in Montserrat (Bold, ExtraBold, Black), body and interface text in Open Sans (Regular, SemiBold, Bold) and data and code in JetBrains Mono, with the fallbacks of Appendix J. Inter, Roboto, Arial, Lato and system interface fonts shall not be used as primary fonts. Fonts shall be served with the application, not from a third-party service, so that an on-premises installation renders identically.

Type sizes shall be taken from the scale 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 24, 30, 36 and 48 pixels (13 pixels for form labels and breadcrumbs), with the hierarchy of Appendix J; hierarchy shall be carried by weight and color, not size alone. Eyebrow labels shall be bold, uppercase and letter-spaced.

Spacing shall be taken from the scale 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 and 96 pixels, on a vertical rhythm of multiples of 8 pixels, in a container at most 1,200 pixels wide with 24-pixel gutters and page margins of 24 pixels on mobile and 32 pixels on desktop.
Radii shall be 8 pixels for buttons, inputs and menus, 12 pixels for cards, 16 pixels for dialogs and 6 pixels or a circle for badges and avatars; no fully rounded (pill) button shall be used.

Elevation shall use only the card, hover and dialog shadows of Appendix J, tinted with Navy; a card shall have either the card shadow or a Line border, never both; no colored shadow or glow shall be used except on primary buttons.

Icons shall come from the Lucide set only, as line icons with a 2-pixel stroke, at 16, 20, 24, 32 or 48 pixels; filled icons, other icon families and emoji used as icons shall not appear. Icon badges shall be solid circles (Azure or Green for emphasis, Navy or Muted for neutral) with a white icon at 50 to 55 % of the diameter, and one screen shall not color its icons in several accent colors.

Every interactive component shall define its default, hover, focus-visible, active, disabled (40 % opacity, not-allowed cursor), loading (spinner replacing the label, width kept), error and success states where they apply, and never rely on browser defaults. Buttons shall come in the Primary (Azure, Navy on hover), Success (Green), Secondary (Azure outline), Ghost and Danger variants, in sizes of 32, 40 and 48 pixels.

Form fields shall be 48 pixels high with 12-by-14-pixel padding, a Line border and an 8-pixel radius; on focus, a 2-pixel Azure border with a soft ring; on error, a 2-pixel border and a 12-pixel SemiBold message in the Critical status color; read-only fields shall have the Background color and no border. Labels shall be 13-pixel SemiBold Navy above the field, help text 12-pixel Muted below it; a required field shall be marked with an asterisk before its label and an optional one suffixed "(optional)". Forms shall use one column up to 720 pixels, two up to 1,024 and three above, with 24 pixels between fields and 32 between groups, validate on leaving a field, list the errors at the top when there are more than three, and never disable the submit button to prevent errors.

Dropdowns shall share the field style, open a white menu with an 8-pixel radius, the card shadow and a maximum height of 320 pixels, with 40-pixel options, the hover in Azure tint, a check on the selected option, chips for multiple selection and a filter at the top for long lists. Checkboxes and radio buttons shall be 16 pixels and filled with Azure when selected; toggles shall be 36 by 20 pixels, Muted when off and Green when on, with the label after the control.

Dialogs shall have an overlay of Navy at 45 % opacity, a white panel with a 16-pixel radius and the dialog shadow, widths of 560, 720 or 960 pixels, 32-pixel padding, a Montserrat title with a close icon, and actions at the end of the footer with the primary action last; Escape shall close a dialog unless the action is destructive, focus shall be trapped inside and returned on closing. Side panels shall be 320, 400 or 480 pixels wide with a fixed header and footer. Tooltips shall be Navy with white 12-pixel text, at most 240 pixels wide, shown after 300 milliseconds.

Tables shall have a header row in solid Navy or Azure with bold white text, body rows alternating White and Background, Line borders, the hovered row in Azure tint and a selected row in Azure tint with a 2-pixel Azure border on its start edge. They shall offer a Comfortable density (56-pixel rows, 16-pixel cell padding) and a Compact density (40-pixel rows, 8-pixel padding), kept per user, and show 6 skeleton rows while loading.

Motion shall clarify a change, never decorate: 150 milliseconds for hover and focus, 200 for menus and tabs, 300 for dialogs, drawers and page transitions, with the standard and emphasis easing tokens, animating transform and opacity rather than layout. Non-essential motion shall stop when the user prefers reduced motion, and no video shall play automatically.

The layout shall adapt at the breakpoints of Appendix J: below 768 pixels a single pane in which the menu becomes a drawer and tables become cards; from 768 to 1,024 pixels two panes with the menu reduced to icons; from 1,024 pixels three panes (menu, content and an optional context panel); from 1,280 pixels the full layout with wider table columns.

Interface text shall lead with the number or the finding, in plain professional language, active voice and short sentences, without superlatives that are not evidenced, without exclamations or emoji (for example "3 of 4 findings resolved. 1 open." rather than "Great job! Almost there!"). Brand and product names shall be written exactly as their owners define them (for example AI Value: two words, both capitalized), and an application's own product name shall be written the same way on every screen and in every document.

The product logo of the application, or the AI Value logo where the application has none, shall appear as the horizontal lockup in the top bar and in document headers and as the icon alone for the favicon and application icon; it shall respect its clear space and minimum sizes (150 pixels or 35 millimeters wide for the full logo, 32 pixels or 8 millimeters for the icon) and shall never be recolored, stretched, rotated, cropped, outlined or given a shadow or a glow.

Generated documents and exports shall follow the Graphical Chart: Open Sans 11-point Ink body, Montserrat Navy headings, tables with a Navy header row and alternating White and Background rows, 2-centimeter margins, A4 by default and Letter where the region requires it, fonts embedded, hyperlinks and color profile preserved (Navy CMYK 100, 80, 30, 20) and the vector logo never flattened to a bitmap. Spreadsheet exports shall use the Status Scale alone for conditional formatting and the chart series colors of FR-DA-VIZ-02; slide exports shall use a Navy title slide and white content slides.
