The tokens and components shall be maintained as one shared, semantically versioned design system (a code package and the AI Value Design System library), from which every application takes them; each release of an application shall state the version of the Graphical Chart it conforms to, and no visual asset shall be considered final unless it references a token.
Keyboard focus shall stay in the field the user is typing in or operating through every keystroke, dropdown change, validation, saving, state update, re-render and panel change.
No input shall be lost on a validation failure, a panel change or a refresh; a field shall never be reset because its value is invalid.

Every interactive element shall show a visible focus ring (3 pixels of Azure at 35 % opacity, 2 pixels from the element); the tab order shall follow the reading order; every action shall be reachable with the keyboard alone; Escape shall close the topmost overlay.

Code review shall reject the known causes of focus loss: a component defined inside a render function; an unstable key (the row position for reorderable rows, a random or time-based value, or a value derived from changing state) instead of the record identifier and column name; automatic focus that runs again after the first display; an effect that moves focus on every change; form fields re-created on every render; a context value re-created on every render; a field that swaps element type (single-line and multi-line) while in use.

Before a table or form is released, automated tests shall confirm that typing in every free-text cell and changing every dropdown keeps focus, that Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape and the arrow keys behave as in Table 4.49-1, that validation and saving do not move focus, that changing record or panel does not move focus unexpectedly, and that no new console warning appears.

A field shall keep the same component identity, element type, name and identifier for as long as it is in use: no list, row or field key derived from an edited value (C2, C12); no name or identifier generated from the current value (C13); no dialog, drawer, panel, wizard step or form region re-created through a changing key, a component defined during rendering or injected HTML (C4, C14); no field removed from the page because its own value, another value being typed or its validation state changes (C18).

A controlled field shall receive a value of the primitive type it edits, never an object or an array (C6), and shall stay controlled for its whole life, a missing value being normalized to the empty value the component expects rather than switching between undefined, null and a value (C22); the public data shape shall not change to achieve this.

Validation and normalization shall never rewrite the value a user is typing nor move focus (C11, C16); validation shall run when the user leaves the field or at the lifecycle point the screen already uses. Autosave, save, checkpoint and synchronization shall never clear, reset or reinitialize an active form or replace its Active Draft; a form is reset only on an explicit close, cancel, discard or save-and-close (C17).

An asynchronous result — search, autocomplete, remote lookup, server validation, autosave, query result or debounced request — shall update a field only when it answers the current request; a stale result shall be discarded through cancellation, request identifiers or sequence checks (C19). A debounce or throttle shall be a single instance for the lifetime of its component, its pending work cancelled when the component is intentionally removed (C20).

The Active Draft shall take precedence over parent, derived, subscribed and server state while the user edits; external state is merged at a lifecycle boundary only (C21). Switching route, tab, panel or wizard step shall not destroy a form whose draft the user expects to keep (C15). Form libraries shall use their stable field identifiers and shall not rebuild field arrays, re-register fields or reset default values while a user edits (C5). A memoized child shall not receive a callback re-created on each render where that identity disturbs typing (C9).

The pointer, focus, blur, click and change events of dropdowns, comboboxes, date and time pickers, popovers, inline editors and Row Editors shall be ordered so that an interaction completes before its field is blurred, committed, reset, closed or removed (C23).

An Input-Integrity Defect shall be corrected at its cause. The following shall not be accepted as a fix: re-focusing a field after rendering or after a delay; focusing a field after every state update; disabling validation or autosave globally; disabling strict mode, lint rules, tests or type checks; suppressing blur events globally; silencing an error instead of correcting its cause.

A remediation pass for input integrity shall follow the audit of Appendix L: a Typeable Field Inventory covering every screen and shared field component, including custom and third-party date pickers, comboboxes, autocompletes, masked and numeric inputs and rich-text editors; a check of every cause C1 to C23, each confirmed instance recorded and fixed or deferred with its reason, and each absent cause reported as “Checked — no instance found”; the smallest correct change, preserving public component interfaces, routes, API contracts, data shapes, business logic and visual design; a final re-scan of the touched areas; and the report of Table L-3.
